issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to implement a constructor following the attribute order from the UML, but the UML's attribute order (numberOfInscribedStudents, lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfTutors) conflicts with the textual attribute list (which starts with lectureName). The provided solution's constructor uses a different parameter order (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) than the UML. This mismatch between the textual description, UML, and solution constructor parameter order can confuse students about the correct constructor signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute/constructor ordering consistent across the problem statement, UML, template, and solution. Either (a) update the UML in problem_statement.md to list lectureName first (matching the textual list and the solution constructor) and adjust the template constructor guidance accordingly, or (b) change the solution constructor to use the UML's order (numberOfInscribedStudents, lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfTutors). Also ensure the template's constructor stub and any instructions explicitly show the chosen parameter order so students implement the expected signature.
